rothNumber_mul_coprime: r₃(M)·r₃(N) ≤ r₃(MN) for coprime M,N — supermultiplicativity of the Roth number
insights: The ZMod-modular Roth number is supermultiplicative on coprime moduli. Proof is elementary: an AP maps componentwise through the CRT iso; injectivity forces a nonzero step in ≥1 factor. No Fourier/density-increment needed.
Product construction A×ˢB is AP-free in ZMod(MN) because a step d≠0 has e(d)≠0, so at least one coordinate has a genuine 3-AP, forbidden by that factor being AP-free.
This gives an elementary lower-bound tool (weaker than Behrend but self-contained, 0-axiom), iterable over distinct prime factors.
